- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.4) and price drops, model underreacts; add 1–3% buffer to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed; apply 1–2% downward adjustment if sentiment volatility > 0.3.
- When sentiment history shows strong downward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive low sentiment), model often fails to anticipate drop; apply 5–10% downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- Forecast should not exceed 10% above or below 30-day moving average of historical prices unless sentiment strongly supports it.
